edits.find:
The stem strips away fever and gives you an afebrile 3-day-old with irritability, feeding refusal, and tachycardia. Everything in the behavioral pattern is shared by NAS, hypoglycemia, and neonatal thyrotoxicosis. The single value that separates sepsis from all three is WBC 3,000 — leukopenia. NAS produces tremor with a normal WBC; hypoglycemia is excluded by a normal glucose; thyrotoxicosis requires a maternal Graves history. Leukopenia in a neonate reflects marrow depletion by overwhelming infection and is more ominous than leukocytosis. The empiric regimen is ampicillin plus gentamicin — ampicillin for GBS and Listeria, gentamicin for gram-negative coverage.

edits.find:
Name the lesion first, then ask where it started and how it related to the fever. Itchy macules, papules and vesicles arriving in successive crops, so that several stages sit side by side, starting on the trunk and face and spreading to the limbs after a short febrile prodrome, is varicella. The other common exanthems are not vesicular: measles and rubella are maculopapular and spread head to toe, roseola appears as the fever breaks, erythema infectiosum is slapped cheeks then a lacy rash, and scarlet fever is sandpaper with a sore throat.

Being up to date on vaccines does not exclude varicella at age 3. The child has had only the first of two doses (ages 1 and 4), and breakthrough varicella is milder, with lower fever and fewer lesions, exactly the picture here.
